Definition: a feminine diminutive of Drusus (a Roman name); Drusilla, a member of the Herodian family:--Drusilla.
BiblicalUsage: Drusilla was the Jewish wife of Felix the governor, who sent for Paul to hear him concerning the faith in Christ, and trembled with her husband at his preaching about righteousness, temperance, and judgment to come.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that hearing the gospel is not the same as obeying it, because Felix and Drusilla listened and then sent Paul away.
RelatedEvents: Paul Before Felix, Festus, and Agrippa
